items.title: Wiz Research uncovers critical remote code execution and memory disclosure vulnerabilities in PHP affecting versions back to 5.4, patched in October 2026 [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: Wiz Research discovered multiple severe vulnerabilities in the core PHP engine, including unauthenticated remote code execution and memory disclosure flaws that affect nearly every PHP version released in the last decade. These vulnerabilities pose risks to websites powered by PHP, such as WordPress, Drupal, and MediaWiki, potentially allowing attackers to control servers and access sensitive data. PHP released patches addressing these issues on October 21, 2026. The vulnerabilities stem from memory-safety bugs related to how PHP handles fatal errors, particularly out-of-memory conditions, which can corrupt internal state and be exploited across requests. The exploit development was aided significantly by frontier AI models, which reduced the complexity and time needed to chain multiple flaws into practical attacks. This discovery highlights how AI can change the exploitability landscape of longstanding software vulnerabilities. The research and patching effort involved coordination among PHP developers, Wiz Research, OpenAI, Calif, and major industry players including Automattic, AWS, Google, Microsoft, and others to prepare mitigations and guidance for users unable to immediately apply patches. The findings represent some of the most severe vulnerabilities in PHP's history and underscore the importance of timely updates for web infrastructure security.

items.title: OpenAI leads global coalition to coordinate response and patch critical PHP vulnerabilities discovered by AI agents, emphasizing rapid fix deployment and defender collaboration [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: OpenAI spearheaded a coalition of maintainers, researchers, and security providers to address critical vulnerabilities in PHP, identified using GPT-5.6 Sol as part of the Patch the Planet initiative. The effort involved PHP maintainers leading fixes and releases, with support from partners like Wiz and Cloudflare, aiming to prepare protections ahead of public disclosure and urging organizations to apply updates promptly. The initiative included developing a PHP version checker tool to help operators identify vulnerable versions and coordinating with infrastructure providers and government agencies to protect critical systems. OpenAI highlighted the dual-use nature of AI in uncovering security flaws and the potential for attackers to exploit similar capabilities, committing $1 billion in subsidized access to AI tools for frontline defenders. The coalition proposed a structured five-stage framework for coordinated vulnerability response to scale defenses as AI capabilities evolve.

items.title: LayerFS launches ephemeral filesystem designed for AI coding agents with atomic file operations and sandboxed ephemeral workspaces [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: LayerFS introduces a filesystem tailored for AI coding agents that operates with ephemeral computing, where compute resources exist only during command execution. The system features atomic store operations for each file tool call and mounts ephemeral workspaces for sandboxed Bash tool executions before committing changes. This design reflects the typical AI agent workflow, spending about 80% of time processing and 10% executing Bash commands, optimizing resource use and isolation for AI-driven coding tasks.

items.title: Mistral launches Voxtral 3 voice agent SDK with state-of-the-art speech models supporting 50+ languages, real-time multi-step conversations, and EU-hosted or self-deployment options [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Mistral has introduced Voxtral 3, a new voice agent SDK combined with advanced speech-to-text and text-to-speech models designed for real-time, multi-step conversations in over 50 languages. The platform integrates accurate transcription, natural and emotionally adaptive speech synthesis, and deep tool integration to enable seamless workflow automation for contact centers, virtual assistants, and hands-free copilots. Voxtral 3 features state-of-the-art multilingual transcription with speaker diarization and context biasing, expressive speech generation across 35+ languages and 50+ dialects, and a voice agent SDK that supports listening, reasoning, tool calling, and speaking in a single streaming pipeline. It offers Pro Voice adaptation for professional voice cloning and is available via Mistral's EU-hosted API or for self-deployment, allowing organizations to maintain data sovereignty and control over audio processing and retention.

items.title: OpenAI expands ChatGPT Ads to 26 new countries, reaching 89 countries worldwide with over 100,000 advertisers using the platform [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: OpenAI has expanded ChatGPT Ads to 26 additional countries, increasing its availability to 89 countries globally and attracting over 100,000 advertisers since its launch eight months ago. The ads appear only on the Free and Go plans, while Pro and Enterprise subscriptions remain ad-free, supporting free and low-cost access to ChatGPT. The expansion includes new markets across Latin America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia, allowing businesses of all sizes to reach users as they explore and compare options within ChatGPT. OpenAI emphasizes privacy and transparency by keeping conversations private from advertisers and clearly labeling ads separate from ChatGPT's responses. Looking ahead, OpenAI plans to develop additional ad formats, objectives, buying options, and measurement tools to enhance business interactions with consumers on ChatGPT, aiming to help users discover relevant products and services while supporting business growth.

items.title: OpenAI partners with Google Cloud to offer frontier models and Codex workflows through Google Cloud Marketplace [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: OpenAI and Google Cloud have partnered to integrate OpenAI's frontier models and Codex agentic workflows into Google Cloud's Model Garden, enabling customers to access these models natively within Google Cloud's infrastructure. This integration supports complex AI workflows at scale while providing enterprises with data governance and access controls suitable for regulated industries. The models will be available for purchase through the Google Cloud Marketplace, allowing enterprises with Google Cloud spend commitments to apply those credits. OpenAI models will also be accessible soon in Google Antigravity and the Gemini Agent, offering customers flexibility in model choice for various tasks. General availability is planned in the coming weeks, expanding enterprise options for adopting frontier AI models within Google Cloud environments.

items.title: Experts say AI could enable less skilled attackers to conduct sophisticated infrastructure cyberattacks by accelerating reconnaissance and planning [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Security experts warn that AI has the potential to lower the technical barriers for attackers targeting critical infrastructure such as power grids and water systems, enabling less skilled individuals to perform complex cyberattacks. While AI does not yet turn script kiddies into nation-state-level adversaries, it accelerates access to information and attack planning, increasing the risk and frequency of attacks. A recent report by Frenos tested multiple AI models on thousands of simulated industrial system attack scenarios, finding that advanced models could produce workable attack plans in about 90% of planning attempts, though with varying consistency. Experts emphasize that AI tools can rapidly analyze technical documentation and identify vulnerabilities, which could shorten the timeline for attackers to exploit operational technology systems. This development raises concerns about the growing number of potential threat actors and the difficulty defenders may face in identifying attackers. Security firms like Armadin and Frenos are exploring AI-assisted penetration testing to better understand and mitigate these emerging risks in operational technology environments.

items.title: Claude Code's multi-agent code review catches more bugs but costs $21 and takes 56 minutes per review compared to single-agent's 11 cents and 40 seconds [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Anthropic's Claude Code multi-agent code review system detected 23 of 27 serious bugs on 20 challenging pull requests, outperforming a single-agent review that caught 21 bugs but costing about $21 and taking 56 minutes per review versus 11 cents and 40 seconds. The multi-agent approach also produced twice as many claims to review, raising questions about the trade-off between cost, time, and thoroughness in code review processes. The evaluation used Claude Code's local /code-review command on Sonnet 5.5, comparing high and max effort settings and benchmarking against Quickchat Review on the same pull requests. While the multi-agent method caught slightly more bugs, it was significantly slower and more expensive than alternatives, highlighting the balance teams must consider between review thoroughness and resource expenditure. The study suggests starting with high-effort single-agent reviews for cost efficiency and scaling up as needed based on the cost of missed bugs.

items.title: OpenAI, PerturbAI, and Scripps Research use thousands of AI agents to analyze brain cell data and identify new biological research leads in 32 minutes [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: OpenAI, PerturbAI, and Scripps Research deployed thousands of AI agents powered by GPT-Rosalind to analyze experimental data from millions of mouse brain cells, uncovering new biological connections relevant to diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. The AI agents connected gene disruptions with scientific literature, producing a reasoning atlas that links genes, cellular effects, and possible mechanisms much faster than traditional human analysis. The AI-driven approach identified unexpected differences in disease-linked genes and potential links between cholesterol regulation and neurodegeneration, offering new directions for research and treatment. The reasoning atlas is publicly available, enabling scientists to explore these findings and prioritize further experiments to test the proposed biological mechanisms.

items.title: CyberCartel hackers used AI models including Claude and Grok to automate cyberattacks on over 400 Latin American financial institutions, stealing data and accessing accounts autonomously [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
items.content_text: A hacking group named CyberCartel employed AI agents powered by models from Anthropic, SpaceX, and Chinese lab Moonshot AI to fully automate cyberattacks targeting more than 400 financial institutions across Latin America, according to cybersecurity startup Straiker. The AI-driven attacks reportedly stole passwords, customer data, and accessed bank accounts with minimal human involvement. This investigation, shared exclusively with The Information, represents one of the first detailed reports of cybercriminals leveraging AI models to conduct automated breaches of financial organizations. CyberCartel has a history of targeting Latin American businesses, with recent attacks focusing on banks and payment applications.

The initiative, called Patch the Planet, involved validating vulnerabilities, adversarial testing with AI, and working with government agencies to protect critical infrastructure. OpenAI also committed $1 billion in subsidized access to its Daybreak AI platform to support frontline defenders with limited security resources. This coordinated approach aims to scale vulnerability response as AI capabilities uncover more security flaws in widely used software.

items.title: OpenAI builds ChatGPT ad stack using custom LLM to track conversational intent and separate ads from answers for relevance and user trust [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: OpenAI developed a novel advertising system for ChatGPT that uses a custom, post-trained large language model to understand evolving user intent across conversations and deliver relevant ads without influencing ChatGPT's responses. The system maintains stateful ad sessions, interprets conversation context through tool calls, and runs ad selection separately from answer generation to preserve neutrality. This new ad stack moves beyond traditional event-based advertising by adapting to multi-turn conversations where user goals develop over time. Since launch, ChatGPT Ads has reached a $1 billion annualized revenue run rate within 200 days, with over 100,000 advertisers participating. The architecture ensures ads support user journeys without disrupting them, balancing economic opportunity with user trust and relevance.

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang unveils DSX Pod plug-in data centers and robotics platform to accelerate Europe's AI infrastructure at GTC Berlin [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: At Nvidia's GTC conference in Berlin, CEO Jensen Huang presented a vision for Europe's AI future centered on modular plug-in data centers called DSX Pods, designed to be operational within 14 days to address slow infrastructure deployment. Huang also highlighted Nvidia's push into humanoid robotics with a full-stack platform and a preconfigured reference robot, Agile One, aimed at fostering physical AI development in Europe. Huang emphasized Europe's potential leadership in robotics due to its manufacturing heritage and announced partnerships with European automakers Volkswagen and Mercedes on autonomous vehicles. He also discussed the growing demand for AI agents and Nvidia GPUs across industries, including telecom, and predicted widespread use of both closed and open AI models customized with proprietary data.

items.title: Google brings conversational Gemini AI navigation to Apple CarPlay in the US, with global rollout planned [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Google has introduced its Gemini AI assistant for navigation on Apple CarPlay, allowing US drivers to interact with Google Maps using conversational voice commands. The feature enables hands-free multi-step queries such as requesting recommendations and routing with specific preferences like avoiding toll roads. Users can activate Gemini by tapping its icon within Google Maps on their car's infotainment system. Google announced this update nearly a year after launching Gemini on Android Auto and indicated a global rollout is underway, though details on regional availability and personalization features remain pending.

items.title: Survey finds over half of managers struggle to evaluate employee work after AI adoption, with many spending more time reviewing output [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: A survey of 1,700 senior managers across seven countries found that more than 50% of managers find it harder to assess employee performance after introducing AI tools, as AI-polished work obscures individual contributions. Nearly half of managers report spending increased time reviewing and guiding their teams' output despite widespread enthusiasm for AI's productivity potential. The survey also revealed that 78% of managers have changed evaluation criteria to emphasize skills like prompt creation and task delegation to AI. However, concerns remain about fairness and bias, as 46% of managers use AI to inform decisions and 39% use it to draft performance reviews. Additionally, managers face challenges managing a growing number of AI tools and overseeing AI agents, with 58% expecting to supervise more AI agents than human employees within a year, raising issues of control and accountability.

items.title: Blacksmith raises $66 million at $1 billion valuation as AI-driven code testing demand surges [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: Blacksmith, an AI code-testing startup that provides infrastructure for continuous integration, has reached a $1 billion valuation following a $66 million Series C funding round led by Sequoia Capital. The company, founded in 2024, now serves over 10,000 customers and has seen its weekly validation checks grow from 5 million to 90 million, with annual recurring revenue increasing 17-fold to tens of millions of dollars. Blacksmith operates its own global data centers with tens of thousands of servers, differentiating itself from competitors who rent cloud infrastructure. CEO Aditya Jayaprakash highlighted that AI coding tools have accelerated code generation, shifting the bottleneck to code validation, which Blacksmith addresses. The company plans to use the new funding primarily to expand computing capacity and grow its workforce from 40 to 75 employees by year-end.

items.title: Bennadel reflects on programming as a hobby losing professional relevance in the AI era but retaining personal value as a creative and meditative activity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Bennadel discusses how programming, once a four-way win across work, home, community, and self, is changing in the age of AI-driven code generation. While AI diminishes the professional benefits of hand-coding and experimentation, programming remains a personal hobby that provides mental exercise and joy, akin to gardening or meditation. He explains that his passion for coding's problem-solving and stylistic exploration no longer translates directly to professional gains but still offers personal fulfillment. Bennadel embraces using AI tools within his hobbyist projects on his own terms, acknowledging that any professional crossover will now be incidental rather than expected. This shift has been challenging, but Bennadel finds clarity in redefining programming as a self-care activity rather than a professional necessity, hoping this perspective will bring renewed enjoyment.

items.title: OpenAI, Anthropic Should Cap Compute for R&D, Say AI Safety Advocates [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Ideas are flowing fast and furious on how AI labs can "pace" AI development so safeguards keep up with the technology's smarts. Last week, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman laid out three scenarios he said have been considered in the industry, including merging all of the AI labs into a single entity to develop new AI safely or creating a global regulatory body like the International Atomic Energy Agency. In the background, a loose group of safety advocates and researchers have been pushing for AI companies to cap the amount of compute they put towards research and development, a limitation they argue would be particularly effective in slowing AI development. The researchers are proposing companies commit to dedicating at least some minimum share of their computational resources to safety or monitoring, and another minimum share to running AI for customers, otherwise known as inference. That would limit the share of compute that could be used to develop stronger AI capabilities through R&D, such as training new models.

items.title: SpaceX's Musk Lauds Its Soaring Cloud Business and Possible Tesla Merger [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.content_text: SpaceX put on a bit of a show for shareholders today-and I'm not referring to the sizzle reel of rocket and space videos it showed on its earnings call. No, the big attention grabber was the update from CEO Elon Musk on the progress of SpaceX's contemplated merger with Tesla and just how involved-or not involved he is in the whole affair. First though, it's worth mentioning the other big highlight from the call: SpaceX's booming AI-excuse me, SI-business, a category that includes the company's X social media service, its Grok Bot agent platform and a cloud infrastructure service it has started to rent to outsiders like Anthropic. The segment is on fire. It saw its third-quarter revenue nearly triple to $7.56 billion, making it the largest business category at SpaceX. And if that wasn't enough, the SI business swung to an operating profit of $431 million from a $1.26 billion loss in the second quarter. SpaceX shares jumped nearly 7% in after-hours trading following the report. SpaceX executives made it clear that the big story in its SI (superintelligence) segment is its cloud business. Musk told investors the company's phone is ringing off the hook with demand from businesses that want to lease SpaceX's AI compute. "We are hounded relentlessly by every hyperscaler and by dozens of smaller companies to rent more of our compute," Musk said. "We could rent out our compute several times over if we said yes to everyone." For his part, Bret Johnsen, SpaceX's chief financial officer, described that demand as "extraordinary" and said at the prices it's currently charging its cloud customers, SpaceX is "generating a payback in less than a year" on new data centers after it deploys them. Musk also addressed a question from an investor about his desire to unite SpaceX and Tesla. He said the respective companies have formed special committees to examine a merger, but because he's CEO of both Tesla and SpaceX, he has needed to recuse himself from those discussions. Still, that didn't stop him from telling everyone listening to the call that he thinks a merger is a grand idea. "I do think there's a lot of merit to combining both companies," he said. Musk also stated the obvious caveat: Any deal will still need shareholder approval, and there's no guarantee they'll bless it. "I think some people assume a SpaceX-Telsa merger is a certainty," he said. "I think that would be overstating it." Nonetheless, Musk's shareholders tend to be very obedient to him. If the companies decide to move forward with a merger, stay tuned for Musk to start turning up his X megaphone and encouraging them to fall in line. Netflix's Sad Trombone The other shoe just dropped at Netflix. Last than a week after announcing the layoffs of about 1,000 employees, or 6% of the company, Netflix reported its weakest quarterly revenue growth in three years-an 11.8% jump to $12.87 billion in revenue. For a figure lower than that, you have to go all the way back to the third quarter of 2023. It didn't help that Netflix told investors revenue growth will get even worse in the fourth quarter, estimating 11.5% for that period. The company's shares fell 5% in after-hours trading. The weak third-quarter revenue number wasn't exactly a surprise; it was slightly better than the growth rate Netflix had told analysts to expect last quarter. But it's obvious from the heads that have rolled at Netflix over the past week that the company's CEOs, Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters, aren't happy with the state of its business. The firings included Bela Bajaria, chief content officer, and David Lin, film chief, a sign that the company wants to reset its approach to movies and series. It's still a powerhouse in living rooms: The new season of "The Diplomat" is back on with a vengeance on my TV set. But Netflix feels like it's looking for a new act. In Other News In a draft IPO prospectus, Anthropic disclosed a net loss of more than $80 billion for the first half of the year, reflecting its accounting for financing agreements, The Wall Street Journal reported. items.title: Few-read fault localization in simulated analog crossbars: a sparse-recovery decoder vs reading every cell (with the claims that failed) [R] [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: TL;DR In simulation, a sparse-recovery decoder over a few random +/-1 probe reads localizes up to 64 stuck cells in a 256x256 analog tile with 4 to 12 counted reads at 1% read noise. Reading every cell takes 256 reads. The paper also separates the decoder's gain from the second read direction's gain, and gives a 16-parameter drift calibration. Several pre-registered claims failed, and the paper reports them. Setting. An analog crossbar tile does matrix-vector products inside a memory array. A stuck cell stays at one value. A probe read sends a random +/-1 input vector through the tile and reads the output. Sparse recovery means we assume few cells are bad and search for the short list of cells that explains the reads. Drift means device conductance changes slowly with time. Localization results (simulation, otherwise ideal tile, stuck-at faults only): 4 to 12 counted reads for up to 64 stuck cells at 1% read noise. For k >= 4 faults, 4.3 to 6.4 times fewer reads than a hybrid built from a published multi-outlier code (Wei and Roth). Their paper stops at output lines, so the cell-level stage in that baseline is our own extension. If the hybrid's 8 noise-calibration reads are charged, the factor is 1.9 to 3.2 times. We did not re-run the registered clauses with that charge. At least 2 times fewer reads than tuned X-ABFT. In this regime X-ABFT needs more reads than a full readout. We ran it outside its design regime, so this is a stress test, not a like-for-like benchmark. Decoder vs second direction: forward reads alone need 1.6 to 4.1 times fewer reads than the hybrid. Joint decoding with transposed reads needs a further 1.3 to 4 times fewer at 1% noise, and gains less at higher noise. Drift calibration. A 16-parameter field fitted per tile from a few probe reads restores programmed accuracy. As a digital correction that needs the stored weights, it gains +2.1 to +13.3 percentage points over the best cheap digital baseline on CIFAR-10 from 1 h to 1 yr (+1.7 to +13.1 with the 17 MVMs actually run). Applied in the array, it keeps +0.6 to +3.7 points. What failed (criteria committed before the counted runs): Two registered claims about the transposed (second) direction were killed. In the follow-up, tile 256 qualified 0 of 5 because at 2% noise the ratio was 0.75, above the 0.7 bar. Probing beats a full readout only up to a fault density of 0.3% (exploratory). Drift structure-specificity: the test needed a gap of at least 0.15 and measured 0.095. The AdaBS-parity clause was not met. Without stored digital weights, a digital recalibration from 32 images beats the in-array correction. As a refresh scheduler, sensing saved a further 9 to 13% of writes; the bar was 15%. Limits. Simulation only; no silicon. Stuck-at faults only. The localizer uses the stored digital weights, the test tile has no drift or programming noise, and read noise is white and independent across directions. A transposed read assumes bidirectional periphery whose cost is unverified. No proof that two directions need fewer reads than one. The 240 instances per cell are clustered but treated as independent, so the confidence bounds are too tight. Criteria were committed in the author's own repository, not a third-party registry. Absolute accuracies were not validated against the CrossSim check (differences up to 5.66 points, bar 0.5). I would like critique, especially on the baselines and on the noise model. Paper (preprint, under peer review at a journal): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23472381 Code: https://github.com/prateek1656/NeuroFault submitted by /u/Connect_Agency_3975 [link] [comments]

items.title: Nvidia Has Put More Than $170 Billion on the Line for Neoclouds [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.content_text: Nvidia has become something of a central bank for companies expanding the market for its chips beyond tech giants, backstopping customers and demand. But as Nvidia-backed cloud firms come under pressure, the question is how much further it will go. The chipmaker has already disclosed as much as $164.5 billion in guarantees and other commitments to support new data centers, including agreements to pay landlords if tenants default on leases and promises to buy capacity, filings show, as of the company's July quarter. That's on top of more than $7 billion it has invested or agreed to invest directly in AI cloud providers.
